inputs.name: d entering as s x d

values.passage_attribution: L18-L26 sit between 'I asked Claude Athos' (L17) and 'I also asked the Red Team' (L27): Athos output relayed by Day (rule U); the source map lists L22 as Day

day.reading: the threshold shrinks as N_e grows, so the models predict the strongest selection ever in modern humans, which is empirically wrong; selection works through differential survival, which d measures and neither Wright-Fisher nor Moran contains
day.holds: the thresholds are correct as stated (5e-5, 5e-8, 6.25e-9 printed as ~6e-9); neither model has an N_e at which selection is impossible (L19)

critic.reading: |s| > 1/(2N_e) is a drift-versus-selection visibility criterion (ChatGPT, L29: N_e s << 1); it says which s drift does not swamp, not how large realised differentials are
critic.holds: Day's own L13 assigns N_e to drift and d to selection, the same split; if d enters as s x d (M-107) the condition reads |s d| > 1/(2N_e), i.e. 4.2e-7 at N_e = 8e7 and d = 0.015, so a small d is a small effective s inside the standard threshold

notes: Model-choice. The arithmetic holds on both readings; the dispute is what the threshold measures. Whether s x d is the right way to carry d into the threshold is not shown in held text beyond the formulas M-107 cites. The passage is model output relayed by Day (rule U), as is ChatGPT's answer.
